front_question: How do Nagara and Dravida temple spires structurally differ from each other?
back_answer: Nagara (North Indian) spires feature a beehive-shaped curvilinear tower called a Shikhara topped by an Amalaka. Dravida (South Indian) towers feature a stepped pyramidal tower called a Vimāna enclosed by massive gateway towers (Gopurams).

front_question: How did historical stepwells like Rani ki Vav combine utility with environmental engineering?
back_answer: Stepwells harvested and stored seasonal monsoon rainwater underground in arid regions. Subterranean multi-tiered stone corridors shielded water from solar evaporation, kept temperatures cool, and served as public community hubs.
